content.value_statement: Writing clear business email takes time and can vary by audience. This skill provides structured templates, tone guidance, and checklist support for polished messages.
actual_capabilities: Drafts professional email structures with subject, greeting, body, call to action, and sign-off.
Provides scenario templates for requests, follow-ups, technical updates, support replies, meetings, apologies, and announcements.
Adjusts tone for formal, casual, urgent, and professional contexts.
Suggests subject line quality improvements using clear examples.
Supplies an email checklist covering recipients, attachments, tone, proofreading, and next steps.
limitations: Does not send email or connect to mail accounts.
Does not verify facts, delivery status, or recipient details.
Requires user-provided context for accurate names, dates, and commitments.
Does not provide legal, compliance, or HR approval for sensitive messages.

use_cases.title: Request Customer Information
use_cases.description: Create clear requests for updates, decisions, or missing details while maintaining a professional tone.

use_cases.title: Announce Technical Changes
use_cases.description: Draft maintenance notices and migration updates with impact, timing, and required actions.

use_cases.title: Handle Support Replies
use_cases.description: Respond to customer issues with empathy, resolution steps, timelines, and escalation paths.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Simple Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a basic business request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a professional email requesting [information] from [recipient]. Tone should be [tone]. Include these points: [points].

prompt_templates.title: Write a Follow-Up
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for a message after a prior email.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a follow-up email about [topic]. Mention the previous message sent on [date]. Keep it concise and include a clear next step.

prompt_templates.title: Respond to a Customer Issue
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for a customer support reply.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compose a customer support reply for [issue]. Acknowledge the problem, explain the fix, give a timeline, and invite follow-up questions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Stakeholder Update
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for a multi-part project email.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an executive email update about [project]. Include status, risks, decisions needed, owners, deadlines, and a direct call to action.

output_examples.input: Need a polite follow-up about an unpaid invoice due last Friday.
output_examples.output:
Subject: Follow-up on invoice payment

Hi [Name],

I am following up on invoice [number], which was due on [date]. Could you confirm the payment status and expected processing date?

Best regards,
[Your name]

output_examples.input: Announce a two-hour API maintenance window to integration partners.
output_examples.output:
Subject: API Maintenance Window - [Date]

Hi [Name],

We will perform scheduled API maintenance on [date] from [time] to [time] [timezone]. During this window, API endpoints may be unavailable.

Please notify affected teams and confirm that retry logic is enabled.

Thanks,
[Your name]

output_examples.input: Apologize to a customer for a delayed order and explain the next step.
output_examples.output:
Subject: Update on Your Order

Hi [Customer name],

I apologize for the delay with order [number]. We have confirmed the cause and expect shipment by [date].

Thank you for your patience. Please reply if you need any changes before shipment.

Best regards,
[Your name]

best_practices: Provide the recipient relationship, purpose, key facts, deadline, and preferred tone.
Review names, dates, links, and commitments before sending.
Ask for a revised version when the tone, length, or call to action feels wrong.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to invent commitments, approvals, or policy statements.
Do not send generated email without checking recipient details and attachments.
Do not use urgent language unless the message has a real deadline.

faq.question: Can it send email for me?
faq.answer: No. It only drafts text that you review and send through your own email system.

faq.question: Does it support customer support messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes support reply patterns for issue acknowledgment, resolution steps, timelines, and follow-up options.

faq.question: Can I choose the tone?
faq.answer: Yes. You can request formal, casual, urgent, friendly, or another professional tone.

faq.question: Will it verify facts in my message?
faq.answer: No. You must confirm names, dates, order details, policies, and commitments before sending.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it rewrite an existing draft?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the draft and explain the desired tone, length, audience, and outcome.
